discipline: Refute, do not confirm. The subject's sole deliverable is a measurement of what leftover-design remains on OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING after D-241, so the measurement was attacked at its completeness rather than its wording. Every digest cited anywhere in the file was recomputed from disk. The authoring artifact the subject rests on (g21-fixture-corpus.v1) was read for what it declares it did NOT author, and that list was set against the subject's enumerated remainder. The controlling passProperty in the occupancy the subject itself cites was read in full and compared against the subject's paraphrase of it. The structurally identical sibling join in the G23 lineage — a leftover-join written at the same position, immediately after a corpus that authored implementations but not their platform copies — was read as a precedent for what a correct remainder must carry, and the on-disk fixture trees of both lineages were listed to test the claim physically.
decisionRule: ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. One MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX stand, so the verdict is REJECT.

mustFixFindings.title: The FX-AUTHORING remainder omits the per-D-002-platform copies of the authored NT-1/NT-2 bytes, and the passProperty paraphrase that would expose the omission is truncated.
mustFixFindings.charge: The subject asserts without qualification that 'leftover-design of NT-1 and NT-2 implementations is stale as an authoring claim' and then enumerates the surviving remainder as exactly the unauthored classes — live-cell crash/panic/timeout/resource/malformed/truncated/duplicate/EOF/process-tree/recovery, CC-1..CC-11, NT-6, and FC-NC-CA1-PROCESS-TREE. That enumeration is presented as exhaustive in three separate live fields. It is not exhaustive. The per-D-002-platform copies of the two payloads corpus v1 did author remain unauthored leftover-design, and the subject does not carry them anywhere. The strings 'platform' and 'D-002' occur zero times in the subject.
evidence: g21-fixture-corpus.v1 (861bb4e7…, pinned by the subject, recorded D-241) lists in whatIsNotAuthored: 'per-platform copies of these bytes'. It is listed among what the corpus did not author, not among what it routed to execution.

That corpus's authoredCatalog.executionRemains routes only 'Candidate-buffer digest, subsequent-session view, and host-projection goldens' to G21 execution. Per-platform copies are absent from it. Under D-056 Decision clause 5 — the clause the subject itself quotes — authoring fixtures remains design work, so unauthored copies that were not routed to execution remain leftover-design.

harness.DR-G21.component-failure-containment.v4 (13addb3c…, the occupancy the subject cites as current) states passProperty: 'Once independently pinned fixture implementations exist for every named corpus class, every live retained-evidence member, every CC-1..CC-11 class, DR-133 NT-1/NT-2/NT-6, and FC-NC-CA1-PROCESS-TREE, for every admitted external component identity ON EVERY D-002 PLATFORM, each retained-evidence member's passProperty holds.'

The subject's obligations[3].reason paraphrases that same clause as 'Occupancy v4 passProperty still requires independently pinned implementations for every named class before execution.' The paraphrase drops the 'on every D-002 platform' qualifier — the one clause under which the omitted remainder is visible.

On disk, docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/g21.v1/ contains exactly two files, one payload per class, with no platform dimension: G21.nt1.unknown-Finding-frame.json (b9ff9338…) and G21.nt2.extra-finding-member-on-closed-payload.json (bc264fc7…).

The structurally identical sibling, g23-leftover-join.v7 — written at exactly this position, after g23-fixture-corpus.v3 authored the implementations but before g23-fixture-corpus.v4 authored the copies — states the remainder correctly: 'Corpus v3 whatIsNotAuthored lists per-platform copies of these bytes among items it did not author, not among executionRemains. leftover-design of those per-D-002-platform copies therefore remains.' It also restates existingGate as 'none as per-D-002-platform copies of authored implementations'. The subject instead carries v4's pre-authoring existingGate string 'none as authored implementations' unchanged.

The G23 lineage's on-disk tree confirms the copies are a distinct authoring act: fixtures/g23.v4/ carries linux-arm64, linux-x86_64, macos-arm64 and macos-x86_64 subdirectories, each holding a copy of all four payloads, and required its own recording at D-239.
mustFixFindings.whyMustFix: This artifact's entire deliverable is the leftover measurement, and the measurement asserts a discharge that has not occurred. The defect also propagates in the one direction that matters: a successor join that authors the remaining classes and reads this enumeration as complete would flip OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING to leftoverDesign false while per-D-002-platform copies of NT-1 and NT-2 are still owed — which is precisely the transition g23-leftover-join.v8 was only entitled to make because g23-fixture-corpus.v4 had first authored the copies and been recorded at D-239. Understating a remainder is the failure mode this join class exists to prevent.
mustFixFindings.repairDirection: State that leftover-design of the per-D-002-platform copies of the authored NT-1 and NT-2 payloads remains, in leftoverDesignOpenStanding and in obligations[3], and carry it in the FX-AUTHORING remainder alongside the unauthored classes. Quote the occupancy v4 passProperty's 'on every D-002 platform' qualifier rather than paraphrasing it away, and restate obligations[3].existingGate so it no longer reads as the pre-authoring string. The repair must not invent a D-002 platform list, must not author the copies, and must not name any platform — g23-leftover-join.v7 carries this remainder without doing any of those things. OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING stays leftoverDesign true either way; what changes is that its remainder becomes truthful.

decision.scopeOfReject: This REJECT is of g21-leftover-join.v5 as a CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED design-contract candidate that binds NOTHING. It changes no live standing. DR-G21 stays OPEN, DR-114 stays OPEN, DR-133 stays OPEN, DR-102 keeps its existing SATISFIED standing untouched, required-now stays 28, leftover-design of OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING remains, and frozen leftover-join.v4 remains the recorded current G21 leftover-join at D-196 until a successor is recorded.
decision.rationale: Custody is clean and the great majority of the subject survives attack: the subject is unmoved at its expected digest and mode, all 61 recomputed digests match live bytes, head and the file 08 pin agree with live HEAD e6d26a73…, required-now is 28 against the live condition-4 row, the DR-G21 token is OPEN, the corpus lists are byte-identical to the live harness, the DR-114 ledger is quoted exactly as doctor-actor leftover-join.v11 carries it, DR-102 is untouched, the naming parent is correctly D-145 / naming v6 rather than leftover-join.v4, no identifier or fixture byte is invented, and the two authored members are correctly named against corpus v1 and against the files on disk. What fails is the one thing this artifact exists to state. The subject declares leftover-design of the NT-1 and NT-2 implementations stale as an authoring claim and then enumerates the survivors as exactly the unauthored classes, in three live fields, with no mention anywhere of the per-D-002-platform copies that corpus v1 explicitly did not author and explicitly did not route to execution, and that occupancy v4's passProperty requires on every D-002 platform before the harness can be executed. The subject's own paraphrase of that passProperty drops the platform qualifier, and its existingGate string is carried over unchanged from the pre-authoring v4 rather than restated. The sibling written at exactly this position in the G23 lineage carried that remainder explicitly, without naming a platform and without authoring anything, and only the following join was entitled to retire it after a separate corpus and a separate recording had authored the copies. Understating a remainder is the failure this join class exists to prevent, so it is MUST-FIX rather than advisory. Alongside it, the join that measures DR-133's negative-test surface carries no DR-133 non-satisfaction guard at all, where corpus v1, D-241 and both G23 sibling joins carry one; that is a guard omission rather than a false claim, and is SHOULD-FIX. One MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX stand, so under the decision rule the verdict is REJECT.
